videos.title: Will the Union Vote Pass Easily? 'Backlash from DX Division Over Performance Bonuses' is the Wild...
videos.subtitle_summary:
1. Samsung employees have expressed significant discontent over performance bonuses, which vary up to 100 times. The union vote on the tentative agreement will determine if this dissatisfaction will impact the outcome. The Samsung joint labor committee will conduct an electronic vote for the union members' approval or rejection of the tentative agreement from March 28 to April 6. Both the main Samsung union and the affiliated unions that temporarily withdrew will have voting rights. If more than 97,000 employees approve, the agreement will be binding for all employees.
2. The primary factor in the approval vote is the backlash from the DX division (50,000 employees) over performance bonuses. While the semiconductor DS division incurs losses but receives large compensation, the smartphone and home appliance divisions make profits but only receive 600 million won in company shares as bonus. This has led to significant dissatisfaction among DX division employees.
3. The second factor is internal conflict within the semiconductor DS division (78,000 employees). The DS division consists of the memory business unit (28,000 employees), foundry LSI, and other common organizations. The high-performing memory business unit questions why their success should be shared with loss-making divisions. Meanwhile, there is also dissatisfaction among low-performing divisions within the DS division over the significant difference in performance bonuses. Despite these issues, it is expected that more than half of the union members will approve the agreement, provided that the tentative agreement includes measures such as raising wages and abolishing the performance bonus cap. Resolving the internal conflicts and unifying the entire Samsung workforce remains a challenge for all parties involved in the negotiation process.
